mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz A-Class A250 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for an A250 typically costs between £800 and £5,000 depending on the engine code and condition. Used M270 units start from £800-£1,800, reconditioned from £2,000-£3,500, and fully rebuilt M260 engines from £2,800-£5,000. Labour for supply & fit adds £400-£800.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mercedes-Benz A-Class A250 have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: All A250 engines use timing chains, not belts. The M270 (W176) and M260 (W177) both have timing chains designed to last the life of the engine with proper maintenance. However, the M270 is known for timing chain stretch on higher-mileage units - a metallic rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Mercedes-Benz A-Class A250?

acceptedAnswer.text: On M270-equipped A250 models (W176, 2012-2018), the most common symptom is a metallic rattling noise from the engine on cold start. Other signs include loss of power, rough idle, hesitation, and the engine management light illuminating. If you hear any unusual sounds, have the timing system inspected immediately - ignoring the rattle can lead to catastrophic engine failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz A-Class A250?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation and condition. A W176 A250 is typically worth £5,000-£15,000 - a rebuilt M270 engine (£2,500-£4,500) can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. A W177 A250 is worth £12,000-£25,000 - a rebuilt M260 engine (£2,800-£5,000) is usually well within the car's value. Always compare the cost of repair against the car's market value.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the M270 and M260 engines in the A250?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M270 is Mercedes' original 2.0-litre turbo petrol engine used in the W176 A250 (2012-2018), producing 211-218 hp with a timing chain. The M260 is a further development of the M270 used in the W177 A250 (2018-present), producing 224 hp. The M260 features improved efficiency and, in later models, 48V mild-hybrid assistance.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz A-Class A250 to misfire?

acceptedAnswer.text: On M260-equipped A250 models (W177, 2018-present), misfires are most commonly caused by cylinder head failure - particularly on cylinder 2. The cylinder head can deform when hot, breaking the seal and allowing valves to burn. Fault codes P1CEF85, P030085 and P030285 are common indicators. On M270 models (W176), misfires are more often caused by timing chain stretch or carbon buildup.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz A-Class A250 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The A250 badge arrived with the third-generation W176 A-Class in 2012 as the range-topping petrol model (excluding AMG), using Mercedes' own 2.0-litre M270 turbocharged engine producing 211 hp. It was replaced in 2018 by the W177-generation A250, which introduced the M260 2.0-litre engine - a further development of the M270 with increased power and improved efficiency. The A250 badge has consistently represented the performance-oriented petrol option in the A-Class range.

milestones.description: M270.920, 2.0L turbo petrol, 211 hp (155 kW) - W176 A250 launch; 350 Nm torque; 7G-DCT standard; 0-60 mph in 6.6 seconds
Facelift with revised ECU calibration; power increased to 218 hp
M260.920, 2.0L turbo petrol, 224 hp (165 kW) - W177 A250 launch; 350 Nm torque; 7G-DCT standard; 0-60 mph in 6.2 seconds
M260.920 gains 48V mild-hybrid assistance; +13 hp electric boost; 8G-DCT introduced
Facelift with M260.920 continuing; 48V mild-hybrid now standard

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz A-Class A250 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The A250 has been powered by two generations of Mercedes' 2.0-litre turbo petrol engine - the M270 (W176) and the M260 (W177). Both are performance-oriented units with distinct failure patterns. Rebuilt A250 engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: M270 Timing Chain Stretch - Why the W176 A250 Rattles on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The M270 turbo petrol engine's timing chain can stretch prematurely, causing a metallic rattling noise when starting from cold. The chain tensioner can also fail, allowing the chain to skip timing. A two-stage chain system connects the crankshaft to both camshafts (with variable cam phasers), and a lower chain drives the oil pump and balance shaft. Lifespan is approximately 80,000 miles. Post-2014 models have strengthened timing components.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Best done at first rattle; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M270 with upgraded timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped; bent valves almost certain

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W176 A250 is worth £5,000-£15,000 depending on condition and mileage. For vehicles under £6,000, a preventative chain replacement (£1,200-£1,800) is usually the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. For higher-value examples, a rebuilt M270 with warranty (£2,500-£4,500) offers peace of mind.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the engine on cold starts - especially between 80,000 and 120,000 miles - act immediately. A preventative chain replacement at a specialist saves thousands compared to waiting for failure. Once the chain jumps, piston-to-valve contact is almost certain and engine replacement becomes the only viable option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M270 Mercedes-Benz A-Class A250 engine prices

problems.h4: M260 Cylinder Head Failure - W177 A250 Misfires and Rough Running
problems.rootCause: The M260 engine can suffer from cylinder head deformation, particularly on cylinder 2. Increased wear on exhaust valve seat rings and valve guides can cause insufficiently sealed combustion chambers, leading to rough running, misfires, and high emissions. Fault codes P1CEF85, P030085 and P030285 are common indicators.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with upgraded cylinder head
repairOptions.longevity: Required if head failure has caused bottom-end damage

problems.recommendation: If your W177 A250 develops a misfire - particularly on cylinder 2 - have the cylinder head inspected immediately. A dealer replacement costs £4,000+, but a specialist can often complete the work for £2,500-£4,000. Mercedes has offered extended warranties on some M260 cylinder head failures, so check your coverage before paying out of pocket.

problems.group: M270 & M260 Intake Valve Carbon Buildup
problems.h4: M270 & M260 Intake Valve Carbon Buildup - Direct Injection Deposits
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz A-Class A250 (M270.920 and M260.920, W176 and W177, 2012-present)
problems.rootCause: Direct injection engines like the M270 and M260 suffer from carbon buildup on intake valves because fuel is injected directly into the cylinder rather than washing over the valves. This is especially problematic on vehicles driven predominantly in the city.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove intake manifold, blast valves with walnut media
repairOptions.longevity: Viable; restores performance and fuel economy

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with cleaned intake system
repairOptions.longevity: Only if carbon buildup has caused significant valve damage

problems.recommendation: If your A250 feels sluggish or has reduced fuel economy, carbon cleaning is often the solution. Regular motorway driving helps reduce carbon buildup. A £350-£600 specialist clean is far cheaper than a £2,500 engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for M270 and M260 carbon cleaning and engine replacement for your A250
